A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffusionVL with the same authors, core method, and principal experiments. All pages, equations, figures, and tables are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-conversion experiments, multimodal benchmark results, and decoding and block-size ablations in Tables 1–5 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v3 retains original conversion results and adds mathematical-reasoning evaluations and controlled noise/paradigm ablations in Tables 4–6.

M1.justification: The backbone, two conversion pipelines, masked-token training, block-wise noise, and cached block decoding remain unchanged. The new equations and inference pseudocode clarify the existing procedure. DiffusionVL-CoT adds training data without introducing a different architecture or objective.

E1.justification: v3 adds mathematical-reasoning evaluation on MathVista, MathVerse, and MathVision, plus training with 100K CoT examples from OpenMMReasoner-SFT. This substantially extends training and task coverage. DetailCaps was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v3 removes the A2D-VL-7B comparison from v1 Table 5. The principal comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged, and LLaDA-V remains the speed comparator. New Table 6 introduces sequence-noise and full-diffusion controls for Qwen2.5VL-7B conversion.

E3.justification: v3 adds math accuracy/throughput comparisons with generation lengths of 64 for LLaDA-V and up to 1024 for DiffusionVL-CoT, matched-backbone noise/paradigm controls, and caption-quality/throughput measurements in the block-size study. Section 4.1 also corrects the stated pretraining-data assignment to LM-based conversions; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 6 tests block-level versus sequence-level noise and block versus full diffusion from the same AR-VLM backbone. The block-size study gains measured throughput and caption quality, and the math experiments investigate CoT finetuning as a response to slow decoding. The existing threshold analysis is mainly redisplayed with fewer reported settings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both already describe speed measurements averaged per device across eight GPUs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and shared Table 3 values are unchanged. v3 adds substantial math and ablation results: Table 4 reports MathVista accuracy/TPS of 64.30/5.21 for DiffusionVL and 63.70/39.47 for the differently trained CoT variant. Removed entries include Table 3's AI2D, MME perception, and base-model BBH scores, the A2D-VL comparison, and selected sensitivity-study results.

T1.justification: Equations (2)–(3) now explicitly sum over masked positions; notably, v1 Equation (3) used an L/D upper limit. This corrects the formal loss specification to match the stated masked-token objective. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The main conversion-feasibility, data-efficiency, SOTA, and headline performance claims remain. v3's conclusion additionally claims efficiency benefits for long CoT generation, extending the claimed application beyond the earlier captioning speed demonstration.

C2.justification: v3 identifies slow math decoding as a limitation, attributes it to missing CoT training data, and presents CoT finetuning as a remedy. It also revises the block-size rationale using measured caption quality and throughput. v1's latent-reasoning analogy and A2D-VL-based interpretation about avoiding annealing disappear.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies AdamW, cosine scheduling, stage/component learning rates, and LMMS-Eval with default prompts. It also documents CoT sampling and math generation limits and clarifies which conversions use pretraining. The model/code access statement remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 removes the A2D-VL citation and the dedicated discussion positioning DiffusionVL against that concurrent conversion method. Related work is substantially expanded with differentiated accounts of existing dVLMs, unified multimodal models such as MMaDA and LaViDa-O, and LLaDA 2.0.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Architecture and modality discussions are merged, inference equations are replaced by pseudocode and revised prose, implementation details gain labeled subsections, speed evaluation becomes a separate section, and the discussion is replaced by conclusion/future-work material.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is completely redrawn, Figure 4 becomes a two-panel captioning/math comparison, and Figure 5 is replaced by Table 7 reporting a subset of its threshold results. Tables are restyled, Table 3 loses columns, the block-size table is restructured, and new math and noise/paradigm tables substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: The controlled ablations, measured block-size speed tradeoffs, and newly disclosed training/evaluation details improve empirical support and reproducibility. These gains are limited by removal of the directly relevant A2D-VL comparison and some conversion results. Unequal generation limits also constrain interpretation of the new math speed comparisons. Overall, v3 provides a modest net improvement while retaining the original headline results.
